AMENDMENT TEXT

Presidential Decree No. 36423 (June 23, 2026)

Enforcement Decree of the Special Act for the Establishment of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special Metropolitan City

[Main body omitted]

ADDENDA

Article 1 (Enforcement date)
This Decree shall enter into force on July 1, 2026. <Proviso omitted>

Article 2 Omitted.

Article 3 (Amendments to other statutes or regulations)
(1) through (28) Omitted.

(29) The Enforcement Decree of the Act on the Management of Zoos and Aquariums is partially amended as follows:

The Honam region row in Annex 2 is replaced by the following.

| Region | Geographic scope |
| --- | --- |
| Honam region | Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special Metropolitan City, Jeonbuk Special Self-Governing Province, Jeju Special Self-Governing Province |

(30) through (78) Omitted.

REASONS FOR ENACTMENT OR AMENDMENT

[Enactment]

Reasons for enactment

The Special Act for the Establishment of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special Metropolitan City was enacted to abolish the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City, respectively, and establish the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special Metropolitan City with a status equivalent to that of Seoul Special Metropolitan City (Act No. 21446, promulgated on March 5, 2026 and entering into force on July 1, 2026). Accordingly, this Decree prescribes matters delegated by the Act and those necessary for its implementation, including special provisions on the operation of autonomous schools, special provisions on the designation of public housing districts, and requirements for designation of investment promotion districts.

Main provisions

(a) Special provisions on general administration

1) Composition and operation of the support committee and working committee (Articles 2 through 13)
The Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special Metropolitan City Support Committee is composed of the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, including the Minister of Finance and Economy, and other members. The working committee is composed of vice ministers of relevant central administrative agencies, including the Vice Minister of Finance and Economy, and other members. Specialized committees for individual fields may be formed and operated where necessary for the efficient operation of the working committee.

2) Special provisions on appointment of state public officials (Article 15)
The Mayor of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City or the Chairperson of its Council may exercise powers concerning appointment, dismissal, disciplinary action, and other appointment-related matters for general-service state public officials of Grade IV or lower and research-service and technical-advisory-service public officials belonging to the Integrated Special Metropolitan City or its Council.

3) Administrative, financial, and budgetary support from the State (Articles 18 and 19)
When implementing policy projects considered necessary for the Integrated Special Metropolitan City, such as fostering regional strategic industries, the heads of central administrative agencies may give priority support to the Integrated Special Metropolitan City and the cities, counties, and districts under its jurisdiction. The Minister of Planning and Budget may provide preferential support to the Integrated Special Metropolitan City when granting subsidies.

(b) Special provisions on educational autonomy

1) Special provisions on operation of autonomous schools (Articles 20 through 22)
The Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City may designate autonomous schools upon application by school principals and after consideration by the Autonomous School Deliberation Committee. The principal of an autonomous school may prescribe the academic year, semesters, number of school days, grade system, and other matters differently from those prescribed in the Elementary and Secondary Education Act. Persons who have graduated from a junior college and worked for at least five years in a field related to the subject they are to teach at certain corporations or organizations, and other eligible persons, may be appointed to autonomous schools as teachers concurrently working in industry and academia.

2) Special provisions on schools for gifted students (Articles 23 and 24)
The Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City designates schools for gifted students upon application by school principals and after deliberation by the City/Do Committee for Promotion of Gifted Education. Every five years, the Superintendent receives self-evaluation reports from the principals of schools for gifted students and evaluates operational performance after deliberation by that Committee. The designation may be revoked if, as a result of the evaluation, the school is deemed unable to achieve its purpose of establishment.

(c) Special provisions on urban development

1) Special provisions on public housing district development projects (Articles 37 and 38)
Powers concerning designation, modification, or cancellation of housing districts, approval of public housing district plans, completion inspections, and other matters for public housing district development projects of at least 300,000 square meters implemented by local public corporations are delegated to the Mayor of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City. Before approving a public housing district development project, the Mayor must consult the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies on the public housing district development project plan.

2) Special provisions on passenger motor vehicle transportation platform business operators (Article 39)
Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City requests support for a project to establish or upgrade a transportation platform, or to expand or improve common facilities or safety management facilities for passenger safety, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may subsidize or lend part of the necessary funds.

3) Special provisions on development of station areas (Article 41)
The Mayor of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City may prescribe building coverage ratios and floor area ratios in development zones differently, within a limit not exceeding 150 percent of the building coverage ratios and floor area ratios applicable to the relevant land-use zones under the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.

(d) Special provisions on industrial revitalization

1) Designation and cancellation of investment promotion districts (Articles 45 and 46)
The Mayor of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City is to designate investment promotion districts primarily in areas where the State or other eligible entities implement development projects covering the whole of an area for which a district-unit plan has been determined, and hold ownership or rights of use over at least two thirds of the land in that area, in order to attract investments such as the establishment of new facilities to conduct research and development business, where the investment amount is at least 500 million won and the number of regular employees is at least ten. The designation is to be cancelled where the purpose of designation cannot be achieved because of a substantial lack of investment progress or in other applicable circumstances.

2) Special provisions on designation of specialized complexes for national high-tech strategic industries (Article 52)
The Mayor of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City may exercise powers to consult and coordinate with the heads of relevant administrative agencies regarding execution and management of budgets supported by the State, approvals and permits, and other matters related to the development and operation of specialized complexes for national high-tech strategic industries.

3) Support for specialized industries in cities, counties, and districts (Articles 57 through 59)
The Mayor of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City is to designate at least one specialized industry for each city, county, or district upon application by the relevant mayor, county head, or district head, or ex officio. Plans to support specialized industries must include measures for technological development, assistance in attracting investment, and other matters. Projects such as the development of industrial complexes and infrastructure may be promoted to foster specialized industries, and their implementation results are to be evaluated regularly.

(e) Other special provisions

1) Scope of special admissions for local talent (Article 69)
The heads of universities located in the Integrated Special Metropolitan City may select graduates of high schools located within the City's jurisdiction and other eligible persons for up to 50 percent of the admission quota of specialized departments operated in connection with regional strategic industries.

2) Special provisions on foreign cultural and artistic professionals and tourism business workers (Article 75)
The Minister of Justice may prescribe different visa issuance procedures and maximum periods of stay for each status of stay for foreign cultural and artistic professionals and other eligible persons working in cultural industry promotion districts, free economic zones, special tourist zones, and similar areas.

3) Special provisions on special historical and cultural zones (Articles 81 and 82)
The Mayor of the Integrated Special Metropolitan City may support activities to transmit intangible heritage and other activities within special historical and cultural zones to protect and foster national intangible heritage. Public institutions, local public corporations, and other eligible bodies meeting specified requirements, including cases of direct necessity for the development and operation of a special historical and cultural zone, may be allowed to use and derive income from public property under negotiated contracts.
